summary: Running for a leadership post: {the post} is open, and {favorite} has most of the votes counted already.
realLife: One life: He ran for House minority leader in 2006 and lost 168 to 27. In 2009 he won the third-ranking post without opposition. Another: The whip appointed him chief deputy whip in 2002. He was elected whip in 2008 and became majority leader in 2011, after raising more than $30 million for the party's House campaigns. Another: Two years into her first term, in 2018, House Republicans elected her conference chair, the third-ranking post.
